title: Exact tensor equivalences preserve the acyclic K-flat test and homotopy categories
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] equipped with tensor bifunctors additive in each variable and countable coproducts. For integer-indexed cochain complexes use the direct-sum total tensor with degree $n$ object $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}X^p\otimes Y^q$ and differential $d_X\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Y$. Let $E:\mathcal A\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:I$ be mutually inverse additive exact equivalences with specified unit and counit satisfying the triangle identities. Write $E_{\rm Ch},I_{\rm Ch}$ for their termwise functors. Suppose natural chain isomorphisms $E_{\rm Ch}\operatorname{Tot}(X\otimes Y)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(E_{\rm Ch}X\otimes E_{\rm Ch}Y)$ and the analogous isomorphisms for $I_{\rm Ch}$ are given. Here exact means preservation of kernels and cokernels. Call a complex acyclic if every $H^n=\ker d^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}$ is zero, a chain map a quasi-isomorphism if every induced $H^n$ map is invertible [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and a complex $P$ K-flat if $\operatorname{Tot}(X\otimes P)$ is acyclic for every acyclic $X$; this is the test in [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-module-kflat-complex] for sheaves and modules respectively. Then $E_{\rm Ch}$ and $I_{\rm Ch}$ are inverse equivalences of complex categories with termwise unit and counit. There are natural isomorphisms $E(H^nX)\cong H^n(E_{\rm Ch}X)$, and likewise for $I$. Both functors preserve and reflect acyclicity, quasi-isomorphisms, K-flatness and K-flat resolutions (quasi-isomorphisms $P\to X$ with $P$ K-flat). They preserve and reflect cochain homotopies, where $u-v=d h+h d$ with $h$ of degree $-1$, and hence induce inverse equivalences $K(\mathcal A)\simeq K(\mathcal B)$ with the same termwise unit and counit. These equivalences commute with shifts and the usual mapping cones: the comparisons use the signed shifted differential and the block cone differential, and carry their canonical inclusions and projections to the corresponding maps. All assertions concern unbounded complexes; the tensor comparisons are isomorphisms of complexes, not merely comparisons of individual cohomology groups.

source.place: Tag 06YN (definition-K-flat), together with more-algebra.tex Tag 06XZ (definition-K-flat); derived.tex section-homotopy: the exact tensor-equivalence invariance argument for the acyclic total-tensor test, cohomology and homotopies, not a theorem asserted by these definitions.

proof.text: For $F=E$ or $I$, define $(F_{\rm Ch}X)^n=F(X^n)$, $d^n=F(d_X^n)$, and $(F_{\rm Ch}u)^n=F(u^n)$. Since $F(0)=0$ and $F(ba)=F(b)F(a)$, these are complexes and chain maps and define functors. Naturality of the given $\eta:1\cong IE$ and $\varepsilon:EI\cong1$, applied to each $d_X^n$, makes their termwise components chain isomorphisms. The two triangle identities hold degree by degree. Thus these functors are inverse equivalences of the complex categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor), exactness via kernels and cokernels; termwise application to complexes

proof.text: For either additive functor $F$, write $\iota_j,\pi_j$ for a binary biproduct's injections and projections [def-sp-abelian]. The maps $b=(F\pi_1,F\pi_2):F(U\oplus V)\to FU\oplus FV$ and $a=(F\iota_1,F\iota_2):FU\oplus FV\to F(U\oplus V)$ are inverse: their products are the identities by $\pi_j\iota_k=\delta_{jk}$ and $\sum_j\iota_j\pi_j=1$, after applying additivity. Also $F0$ is zero since $1_{F0}=F(1_0)=F(0)=0$. Hence $F$ preserves finite products and coproducts. Equalizers and coequalizers are kernels and cokernels of differences; the assumed kernel and cokernel preservation therefore gives finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation. This verifies the exactness convention required by the next cited statement.

proof.text: Use the exact-functor cohomology comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], implemented by ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso for X.sc n. Its naturality lemma gives a natural isomorphism from mapped complex homology to the image of homology; invert it for the displayed direction. Apply this construction to both E and I.

proof.text: At each integer n, ShortComplex.exact_map_iff_of_faithful identifies exactness of the mapped short complex with exactness of X.sc n. Quantifying over n gives preservation and reflection of acyclicity. HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_map_iff_of_preservesHomology gives the analogous quasi-isomorphism equivalence [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The required homology-preservation and reflection instances are supplied by the additive equivalence.

source.place: Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor), exactness via kernels and cokernels; termwise application to complexes

proof.text: A chain isomorphism induces invertible cohomology maps, by applying the cohomology functor to its inverse [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so acyclicity is invariant under chain isomorphism. If $P\cong P'$ then for each $X$, functoriality of the tensor and totalization gives $\operatorname{Tot}(X\otimes P)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(X\otimes P')$, whose inverse is obtained by tensoring the inverse. Thus the acyclic-test definition of K-flatness in the statement is invariant under chain isomorphism as well.

source.place: Tag 06YN (definition-K-flat); more-algebra.tex Tag 06XZ (definition-K-flat). Direct transport of the acyclic total-tensor test through the stipulated chain isomorphisms.

proof.text:
Suppose $P$ is K-flat and $Y$ is an acyclic complex of $\mathcal B$. The previous acyclicity result makes $I_{\rm Ch}Y$ acyclic. The given tensor comparison and termwise counit give chain isomorphisms
$$E_{\rm Ch}\operatorname{Tot}(I_{\rm Ch}Y\otimes P)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(E_{\rm Ch}I_{\rm Ch}Y\otimes E_{\rm Ch}P)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(Y\otimes E_{\rm Ch}P).$$
The complex inside $E_{\rm Ch}$ is acyclic by the defining test for $P$, hence so is the last complex. Therefore $E_{\rm Ch}P$ is K-flat. Interchange $E,I$, and use $I_{\rm Ch}E_{\rm Ch}X\cong X$ from the inverse termwise unit, to prove preservation by $I_{\rm Ch}$. Conversely, if $E_{\rm Ch}P$ is K-flat, every acyclic $X$ has $E_{\rm Ch}X$ acyclic, and
$$E_{\rm Ch}\operatorname{Tot}(X\otimes P)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(E_{\rm Ch}X\otimes E_{\rm Ch}P)$$
is acyclic; reflection of acyclicity gives the test for $P$. Interchanging $E,I$ proves reflection by $I_{\rm Ch}$. The right-hand tensor position of $P$ is unchanged throughout; no symmetry of tensor is used.

Apply and_congr to the quasi-isomorphism equivalence of step 4 and the tensor-test equivalence of step 6. Repeat for I. No specialized sheaf or monoidal K-flat predicate is needed.

proof.text: Functor.mapHomotopy applies an additive functor to the cochain homotopy equations; Functor.preimageHomotopy lifts each component by fullness and reflects its equation by faithfulness. These maps give the two implications on Nonempty homotopies, for both E and I.

source.place: Tag 05RN (section-homotopy), Tag 013H (definition-complexes-notation); homology.tex Tag 0112 (lemma-compose-homotopy-cochain) and the preceding cochain homotopy formula

proof.text: Use the complex equivalence e.mapHomologicalComplex from step 1. Define the unit and counit on a homotopy-category object represented by X by applying the quotient functor to the corresponding complex unit and counit components. NatIso.ofComponents supplies the natural isomorphisms: naturality follows by quotienting complex-level naturality. Every homotopy-category object has a complex representative. Functor.map_comp then turns the two complex triangle identities into the required identities on quotient classes. The component equations hold definitionally.

source.place: Tag 05RN (section-homotopy), Tag 013H (definition-complexes-notation); homology.tex Tag 0112 (lemma-compose-homotopy-cochain) and the preceding cochain homotopy formula

proof.text: For both E and I, use the canonical commShiftIso of mapHomologicalComplex, whose components in every degree are definitionally identities, and the canonical commShiftIso of mapHomotopyCategory. Additivity is exactly what preserves the signed shifted differential.

For both E and I use CochainComplex.mappingCone.mapHomologicalComplexIso. Mathlib map_inr gives the inclusion equation. Its explicit biproduct formula, composed with fst, gives the projection equation by the injection-projection identities and additivity. Mathlib map_δ gives the equation for the negative cone projection and the canonical shift comparison. Finally mapTrianglehIso gives the comparison after quotienting; simplify its construction from mapTriangleIso to check its first two components are identities and its third is the quotient of the same cone comparison [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Each degreewise formula above is defined for every integer, and the total-tensor chain isomorphisms were hypotheses for the unbounded direct-sum totalizations themselves. The K-flat tests in step 6 quantify over all acyclic complexes. Hence none of the conclusions requires boundedness, exactness of countable coproducts, or additional tensor-flatness assumptions.
